defects.description: Route 53 -> CloudFront alias edge is typed kind 'origin'; DNS aliasing is not an origin relationship.
With a private S3 REST origin via OAC, only the distribution's default root object is served; index documents for sub-paths (e.g. /menu/) need a CloudFront Function or flat filenames. Not mentioned.
HTTP-to-HTTPS redirect (viewer protocol policy) not stated; no open questions raised (e.g. who updates content, domain registrar).

reviews.summary: Correct, cheap CloudFront + private S3 (OAC) + ACM(us-east-1) + Route 53 static site with accurate cost and Shield Standard notes; only small modeling gaps.

defects.description: States 'No WAF or Shield is added' without noting that Shield Standard is automatically included for CloudFront; slightly misleading.
Index-document handling for sub-paths with an OAC/REST origin and HTTP->HTTPS redirect not addressed.

reviews.summary: Same correct CloudFront + private S3 (OAC) + ACM + Route 53 pattern with useful open questions; minor explanation imprecision on Shield.

defects.description: Worker node group and ElastiCache are placed only in private subnet A and the ALB in a single public subnet; an ALB requires subnets in at least two AZs and a single-AZ node group defeats the Multi-AZ RDS. The assumption says two AZs but the diagram contradicts it.
No pod-level IAM (IRSA / EKS Pod Identity): pods read Secrets Manager and write to CloudWatch/X-Ray via the node role, so every pod gets every permission; violates least privilege.
No container registry (ECR) modeled or questioned for the 12 service images.
WAF -> ALB edge labelled with protocol HTTPS; WAF is an association, not a traffic hop. MySQL/Redis edges typed 'write' only.
ElastiCache in-transit encryption/AUTH and Redis credentials not addressed (Secrets Manager holds only MySQL creds).

reviews.summary: Sound EKS + RDS Multi-AZ + ElastiCache + CloudWatch/X-Ray + WAF design that meets the brief, but diagrams single-AZ compute and lacks IRSA/ECR.

defects.description: High availability of the shared MySQL and Redis (Multi-AZ, replicas/failover) is left as an open question instead of a default; for a shared datastore serving 12 services this is a reliability gap.
Route 53 -> ALB edge typed 'invoke' with protocol HTTPS; Route 53 only resolves DNS and does not proxy HTTPS traffic.
Public entry point has no WAF by default (only an open question).
ECR left unresolved; ECR->EKS edge direction shows registry pushing to cluster though pulls are initiated by nodes. DB/cache edges typed 'read' while description says reads and writes.

reviews.summary: Good EKS migration design with IRSA, ECR, separate private data subnets and full observability, but HA for data stores and WAF deferred to questions and a DNS edge mis-described.

defects.description: Order lookup by order ID is only satisfied by the table key; no API route / read path (GET /orders/{id}) is modeled.

Dual write: intake Lambda writes DynamoDB then publishes to SNS non-atomically; if publish fails after the write, downstream steps are silently never triggered. No outbox/DynamoDB Streams or reconciliation mentioned.
No explicit alarm on DLQ depth; messages can sit in DLQs unnoticed, weakening 'never silently lost'.

Idempotency of workers under at-least-once delivery only raised for payment as an open question, not designed; customer-managed KMS keys would also require SNS/SQS key-policy grants if extended to queues.

reviews.summary: Clean SNS->SQS fan-out with per-step queues, per-step DLQs, Cognito and KMS, but omits the lookup read path and explicit DLQ alerting and has an unhandled dual-write.

defects.description: Dual write: order Lambda stores in DynamoDB then publishes to SNS non-atomically; a failed publish leaves an order whose steps never run, without any outbox/stream or reconciliation.
Single shared DLQ for three queues makes per-step triage and alarming coarser (redrive-to-source still works).
Cognito -> API Gateway edge direction is inverted (API Gateway authorizer validates tokens issued by the pool). Lambda logs to CloudWatch not drawn.
No open questions (payment provider idempotency, compensation when payment succeeds but reservation fails).

reviews.summary: Covers every explicit requirement incl. GET by order ID, retries via SQS, DLQ with depth alarm and idempotent handlers, with the same unaddressed dual-write risk.

preference.why: Both are the same correct CloudFront + private S3 + ACM + Route 53 design; differences are cosmetic.
B adds IRSA least-privilege and ECR and separates data subnets, whereas A diagrams single-AZ compute and gives all pods the node role, though A is stronger on Multi-AZ RDS and WAF.
B explicitly serves lookup by order ID and alarms on DLQ depth with stated idempotency, while A omits the lookup path and DLQ alerting despite its nicer per-step DLQs.
